plainTranslation: A's love and values meets B's mind. The square puts them in friction.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Imported from project-authored synastry matrix material. Source file was not copied into the repository.
summaryDeep:
This is the quiet distance between what one person says and what the other person needs to feel loved. It lives in a tender, specific place: the gap between being drawn to someone and actually feeling understood by them.

You may find yourself attracted and irritated in nearly the same breath. Something about this person's mind, their humor, the particular way they put things, pulls you in. And then the same mouth that charmed you says something that lands wrong, and you feel the pull and the friction at once, unsure which one to trust.

Sometimes the mismatch is loud. One of you is too blunt, the other too careful. One wants the truth laid bare, the other wants it handled gently. But more often it is subtle, almost too small to name. A compliment that arrives slightly off. A joke that grazes a nerve. A conversation that was supposed to bring you closer and instead leaves one of you a little lonelier than before it started.

Because this touches Venus, it reaches further than conversation. To feel admired, appreciated, understood is part of what keeps desire alive between two people. When words keep missing that mark, something quietly cools. It is rarely a loss of feeling. It is the slow accumulation of small moments where neither of you felt fully met, until the affection has to work harder to stay warm.

The work here is not to flatten yourself into someone more agreeable, or to stop saying what is true. It is to get genuinely curious about what this person experiences as care, which may look nothing like your own version of it. We tend to offer love in the language we would want to receive it, and then feel hurt when it does not translate. What lands as tender to you may read as flat to them. What feels honest to them may feel sharp to you.

This is the slow practice the square asks for. Not better chemistry, you already have that. The harder thing: learning how this particular person receives words, and letting them learn yours. Attraction can survive on its own for a while. What deepens it is the moment one of you stops assuming and starts asking, and the other finally feels seen in the exact place they kept getting missed.
